subject: Post-call technical recap & next steps — SDK auth, routing, embeddings, prompt governance
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@clearvista.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — follow-up & proposed next steps from today

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and actionable next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (very high level):
- Primary use-case: in-product assistant for customer support reps (US + EU) that can surface KB content, call docs via tool-calling, and provide short-form drafts.
- Constraints: PII only in-session, EU data residency for EU customers, strict audit/logging and SOC-2 evidence requests.
- Success metrics: 50% reduction in time-to-first-draft for reps, sub-300ms median token latency on common prompts, stable monthly token spend target.

Technical items we promised to spell out:
1) SDK & auth: recommend using Redwood SDK with short-lived JWT via your auth provider; token exchange pattern (OIDC) to mint service token scoped to account/route. I attached a draft diagram (redwood-auth-routing-draft.pdf).
2) Routing & model variants: route low-latency prompts to hosted small model for autocomplete and larger model for final drafts; fallback to replicas in next region.
3) Structured output & tool-calling: use structured JSON schema + function-calling pattern for KB lookups and ticket creation.
4) Embeddings & reranker: index KB with 1536-d dense embeddings; compute sparse hybrid for recall-critical queries; add a lightweight reranker model for top-10 re-ranking.
5) Prompt governance: versioned system prompts stored in a prompt registry; signed prompt revisions and a red-team playbook for prompt-injection attempts.

Next steps I propose (owners & dates):
- Dev: outline auth flow (OIDC exchange + short-term tokens) and sample SDK snippet — Dev (by Wed 02/17).
- Engineering touchpoint: 60-minute architecture deep-dive (token routing, KV cache, embeddings pipeline) — schedule for Thurs 02/18; Sarah to confirm availability.
- Security/compliance: share SOC2 evidence checklist and recommended audit log retention — Neha (by Fri 02/19).
- Prompt governance doc + versioning proposal — Marcus & Dev (draft by Mon 02/22).

Attachments: redwood-auth-routing-draft.pdf, clearvista-mvp-mapping.xlsx

If that looks good I'll send calendar invites for the deep-dive and drop the auth snippet into the shared Drive.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex/Sarah — happy to join the Thurs deep-dive. Quick replies inline to your questions: 

1) EU residency: Two options — a) Redwood Private in your EU tenancy (recommended for strict residency + audit control) or b) Hosted with region pinning + customer-side encryption + dedicated index instance. Both support the embeddings index living in EU. I'll sketch cost/latency tradeoffs in the call.

2) Okta token exchange for delegated calls: we support the OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693). Flow we recommend: user signs in -> Redwood receives short-lived code -> Redwood exchanges code for short-lived service token scoped to the rep (timeboxed, per-route scopes) -> calls include route header and token context. I'll paste a sample SDK snippet in the Drive doc before the meeting.

3) Rollback & audit for prompts: our prompt registry supports immutable versions (v1, v2...) and a signed changelog. Rollback is a single API call to pin to a previous version; all evaluations and red-team test results are linked to the version id. We can export the audit trail as CSV for your compliance team.

Extra note on reranking: to keep latency low we recommend a two-stage approach: sparse candidate retrieval -> embed top-200 -> rerank top-10 with a small fine-tuned reranker. That keeps median token latency under target while improving precision.

I'll bring a short diagram and sample SDK exchange snippet (pseudocode).

Cheers,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Morning Sarah — short compliance note: the telemetry set you listed looks good. We'll add log-level retention defaults and a recommended HA audit-log configuration in the Drive doc. Regarding red-team + runtime sanitizer:

- Runtime sanitizer: we recommend a layered approach — input validation (reject non-JSON when schema expected), canonicalization of user inputs, token-budgeting guardrails (hard caps per call), and an allowlist for backend tool calls. Our SDK exposes hooks for a "pre-exec" sanitizer that can be deployed at the API gateway.
- Red-team checklist (brief): 1) prompt injection vectors (HTML, JSON, system role overrides), 2) adversarial context stitching, 3) instruction mixing via KB documents, 4) malicious tool-call payloads. We'll share our full checklist and a sample test harness.

I'll upload the telemetry CSV, the SOC2 mapping, and the red-team checklist to the Drive link in the next 90 minutes. See you on the call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
